enterable_display_text:
Commands available in the current context (global):
- go_up
  Change context to the parent of the current context. This could change the commands that are available.

- open_controls_monitor
  Enter ControlsMonitor for control performance, dashboards, and findings by control code. Skip if already in ControlsMonitor or ControlFinding. Not for how risky an entity already in context is (assess_risk).

- open_directory
  Enter DirectoryExplorer so find_* and open_*_by_uid are available. Skip if already in DirectoryExplorer or an entity opened from it. Entry is not the answer — continue with find_*, browse_catalog, or open_*_by_uid.

- open_reconciliation
  Enter the account-to-identity reconciliation workspace.

- reset_context
  Reset the current context to the global context (*). This could change the commands that are available.

- what_can_i_do
  List all the commands available in the current context along with their metadata
  outputs:
  - valid_command_names, type: list[str]

- what_is_current_context
  Show the current context and its properties (if any).

- who_am_i
  Report the acting user, roles and enabled features.

Commands available after entering the ControlsMonitor context (not callable until then):
- list_controls
  List available controls and the codes used to query their findings.
  Before executing list_controls, navigate to ControlsMonitor as follows: open_controls_monitor
- list_findings
  List the current defects for a control.
  Before executing list_findings, navigate to ControlsMonitor as follows: open_controls_monitor
- open_finding
  Open a control finding for detail and action, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing open_finding, navigate to ControlsMonitor as follows: open_controls_monitor

Commands available after entering the DirectoryExplorer context (not callable until then):
- find_account
  Find accounts by login/name and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_account_by_uid then open_portrait) or what logins are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_account, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- find_group
  Find groups by name and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_group_by_uid then open_portrait) or what groups are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_group, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- find_identity
  Find identities by name, login or email and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_identity_by_uid then open_portrait) or what people are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_identity, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- find_organization
  Find organisations/business units by name and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_organization_by_uid then open_portrait) or what orgs are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_organization, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- find_permission
  Find permissions/entitlements by name and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_permission_by_uid then open_portrait) or what rights are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_permission, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- who_has_access_to
  List identities/accounts with access to a named resource from Directory. When already on a Permission, use show_holders instead.
  Before executing who_has_access_to, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- browse_catalog
  Wildcard-find the directory catalog, then portrait a representative
(root organisation when orgs were listed). Requires DirectoryExplorer
(open_directory first if global). Do not call the individual find_*
commands, show_properties, or open_*_by_uid first. If this already ran and
the user repeated the vague request, open the next unused representative
instead of browsing again.
  Before executing browse_catalog, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_account_by_uid
  Open an account by uid after find_account.
  Before executing open_account_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_application_by_uid
  Open an application by uid after find_application.
  Before executing open_application_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_group_by_uid
  Open a group by uid after find_group.
  Before executing open_group_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_identity_by_uid
  Open an identity by uid after find_identity, then use open_portrait. Walk available_from on identity_uid if the uid is missing.
  Before executing open_identity_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_organization_by_uid
  Open an organisation by uid after find_organization.
  Before executing open_organization_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_permission_by_uid
  Open a permission by uid after find_permission.
  Before executing open_permission_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- open_repository_by_uid
  Open a repository by uid after find_repository.
  Before executing open_repository_by_uid, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- find_application
  Find applications/systems by name and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_application_by_uid then open_portrait) or what apps are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_application, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory
- find_repository
  Find repositories/connectors by name and stop at the match list. Not for open/inspect (open_repository_by_uid then open_portrait) or what feeds are on file (browse_catalog).
  Before executing find_repository, navigate to DirectoryExplorer as follows: open_directory

Commands available after entering the ReconciliationWorkspace context (not callable until then):
- list_unreconciled_accounts
  List the accounts of a repository or application with their reconciliation state.
  Before executing list_unreconciled_accounts, navigate to ReconciliationWorkspace as follows: open_reconciliation

Commands available after entering the Application context (not callable until then):
- list_accounts
  List accounts on this application, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing list_accounts, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- list_rights
  List the application's rights, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing list_rights, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- open_group
  Open one of this application's groups by uid.
  Before executing open_group, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- show_app_owner
  Show the application's owner.
  Before executing show_app_owner, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- add_tag
  Add a tag to the current entity.
  Before executing add_tag, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- assess_risk
  Show the current entity's risk score together with the control findings
that drive it. Requires current entity context; if not in one: via go_up ->
open_directory -> find_* -> open_*_by_uid, or in current context. Do not
stop at show_risk_score. Not for why a named finding was flagged
(explain_risk) and not for how to fix (propose_fix).
  Before executing assess_risk, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- list_controls_hit
  List the control violations the current entity triggers.
  Before executing list_controls_hit, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- list_remediation_actions
  List the remediation actions available for the current entity. Only when the request asks for corrections, fixes or remediations; not part of an audit, a look or a walk.
  Before executing list_remediation_actions, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- open_portrait
  Show the current entity's relational portrait in one call. Requires
current entity context; if still in DirectoryExplorer, open by uid first
(via go_up -> open_directory -> find_* -> open_*_by_uid, or in current
context). Do not call show_properties or show_metadata first. Do not go_up
until the user asks. The command already includes the type-specific
relations.
  Before executing open_portrait, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- propose_fix
  List the control findings on this entity and the remediation actions
that could resolve them. Only when the request asks for corrections, fixes
or remediations; not part of an audit, a look or a walk. Requires current
entity context; if not in one:
via go_up -> open_directory -> find_* -> open_*_by_uid, or in current
context. The corrections listed are on offer for the user to apply; this
workflow does not run them. Do not substitute explain_risk.
  Before executing propose_fix, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- remove_tag
  Remove a tag from the current entity.
  Before executing remove_tag, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- show_metadata
  Show custom metadata and tags on the current entity.
  Before executing show_metadata, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- show_properties
  Show the current entity's core attribute fields only. Not the relational portrait (open_portrait) and not a named find.
  Before executing show_properties, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)
- show_risk_score
  Show only the numeric risk score. For how risky this entity is use assess_risk (score plus the findings that drive it).
  Before executing show_risk_score, navigate to Application as follows: open_directory, then open_application_by_uid <application_uid> (needs application_uid)

Commands available after entering the ControlFinding context (not callable until then):
- explain_risk
  Explain why this control finding was flagged. Not for how risky the current entity is (assess_risk) and not for how to fix (propose_fix). show_metadata is not a substitute.
  Before executing explain_risk, navigate to ControlFinding as follows: open_controls_monitor, then open_finding <finding_uid> (finding_uid required to enter ControlFinding)
- show_affected_entities
  List the entities of one family affected by this finding.
  Before executing show_affected_entities, navigate to ControlFinding as follows: open_controls_monitor, then open_finding <finding_uid> (finding_uid required to enter ControlFinding)
- show_metadata
  Show the tags attached to the control this finding belongs to.
  Before executing show_metadata, navigate to ControlFinding as follows: open_controls_monitor, then open_finding <finding_uid> (finding_uid required to enter ControlFinding)

Commands available after entering the Identity context (not callable until then):
- list_accounts
  List the identity's accounts, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing list_accounts, navigate to Identity as follows: open_directory, then open_identity_by_uid <identity_uid> (needs identity_uid)
- list_entitlements
  List the identity's entitlements.
  Before executing list_entitlements, navigate to Identity as follows: open_directory, then open_identity_by_uid <identity_uid> (needs identity_uid)
- list_groups
  List the identity's group memberships.
  Before executing list_groups, navigate to Identity as follows: open_directory, then open_identity_by_uid <identity_uid> (needs identity_uid)

Commands available after entering the Organization context (not callable until then):
- list_identities
  List identities in this organisation, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing list_identities, navigate to Organization as follows: open_directory, then open_organization_by_uid <organization_uid> (needs organization_uid)

Commands available after entering the Repository context (not callable until then):
- list_accounts
  List accounts in this repository, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing list_accounts, navigate to Repository as follows: open_directory, then open_repository_by_uid <repository_uid> (needs repository_uid)

Commands available after entering the Account context (not callable until then):
- list_permissions
  List the account's permissions, and open one if a uid is given.
  Before executing list_permissions, navigate to Account as follows: open_directory, then open_account_by_uid <account_uid> (needs account_uid)
- show_account_custodians
  Show the account's owner and managers together. Requires Account
context; if still in DirectoryExplorer, open_account_by_uid first. If no
manager is assigned, still show the owner. Do not call show_account_owner
or show_account_manager separately. Not the full account portrait
(open_portrait).
  Before executing show_account_custodians, navigate to Account as follows: open_directory, then open_account_by_uid <account_uid> (needs account_uid)
- show_account_manager
  Show the assigned managers of the account.
  Before executing show_account_manager, navigate to Account as follows: open_directory, then open_account_by_uid <account_uid> (needs account_uid)
- show_account_owner
  Show the identity this account is reconciled to.
  Before executing show_account_owner, navigate to Account as follows: open_directory, then open_account_by_uid <account_uid> (needs account_uid)

Commands available after entering the Group context (not callable until then):
- list_members
  List the group's members.
  Before executing list_members, navigate to Group as follows: open_directory, then open_group_by_uid <group_uid> (needs group_uid)
- show_nesting
  Show parent/child group nesting.
  Before executing show_nesting, navigate to Group as follows: open_directory, then open_group_by_uid <group_uid> (needs group_uid)

Commands available after entering the Permission context (not callable until then):
- show_holders
  List identities/accounts holding this permission.
  Before executing show_holders, navigate to Permission as follows: open_directory, then open_permission_by_uid <permission_uid> (needs permission_uid)
- show_sensitivity
  Show the permission's sensitivity/risk classification.
  Before executing show_sensitivity, navigate to Permission as follows: open_directory, then open_permission_by_uid <permission_uid> (needs permission_uid)
